A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDA research. All 28 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including Appendices A–L, support comparison. Relocated analyses and renumbered figures were matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia retraining interventions, induction-head and ICL measurements, synthetic-data augmentation results, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds robustness comparisons, general-performance evaluations, larger-model tracing measurements, and qualitative SAE attribution results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 3 revise the specified induction probe from copy-token log-likelihood to the target head's direct logit contribution over copy positions in repeated sequences. This changes one concrete attribution objective while retaining Algorithm 1, EK-FAC, parameter blocks, and the augmentation pipeline. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained head-emergence, synthetic-copying, and WikiText-2 ICL evaluations, v2 adds WikiText-103 language modeling and PopQA factual-knowledge evaluation (Section 6.3). Appendix L.3 also extends actual attribution experiments to SAE features, previously presented only as a possible framework instantiation.

E2.justification: Appendix G.2 and Figure 10 add evaluated comparators: MDA (Prefix Matching Score), using a QK-only probe, and Controlled Random, controlling n-gram repetition, entropy, and domain. The original baseline and ordinary random comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include OLMo-2-1B/7B tracing and timing without counterfactual retraining, language-modeling loss and factual NLL evaluations on Pythia-31M/70M/160M, and rescoring L3H3's top 100,000 samples across heads. The original training windows, sample counts, batch sizes, and intervention budgets in Tables 4–5 and Appendix E.3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-head projection localization, ranking stability across seeds, QK-only probe ablation, repetition-controlled augmentation, and checks for general-performance side effects (Appendix F.1, G.1–G.2, Section 6.3). It also adds OLMo and SAE qualitative cases. Earlier insertion ablations, head-ablation validation, and multi-head dynamics are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 9 newly reports attribution rankings for three seed configurations, assessed through top-100,000 overlap and Spearman correlation. v1 already mentioned following Pythia seeds and included a 3-sigma comparison. The addition does not establish more repeated retraining runs or introduce uncertainty estimates for the main performance curves.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original intervention curves retain their results. New results include seed overlaps of 0.899–0.907 and correlations of 0.895–0.911, probe/control comparison trajectories, general-performance curves, cross-head projection scores, and OLMo/SAE examples. Table 6 newly reports 80 and 384 A100 GPU-hours for OLMo-2-1B and 7B tracing; these are additions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 replaces the mathematical definition of the induction objective and introduces a previous-occurrence map, copy targets, and valid query positions. This is a non-equivalent formal revision. The influence-function derivation, EK-FAC assumptions, and two information-geometric propositions and proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same core claims: unit-level data attribution, causal effects of selected training data, structural catalysts and ICL coupling, and transferable synthetic augmentation. New evaluations support these existing claims without materially redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 and Appendix F.1 newly distinguish direct unit-local attribution from indirect effects and complete causal mediation. v2 also interprets the QK-only comparison and suggests more abstract structural recurrence in larger models. Section 5.4 corrects the ICL-score interpretation from positive to negative, while Figure 5 explains that the unchanged plots display absolute values.

D1.justification: Table 6 adds architecture dimensions and per-model A100 tracing costs; Appendix E.5 discusses restricting the computation graph and data-parallel tracing. Appendix L.3 identifies the SAE model and feature IDs. Existing Pythia configurations, synthesis prompts, hardware disclosure, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of prior training-time interventions, data-driven generalization, an attribution survey, induction-head ablation work, and circuit decomposition or multiplicity, alongside new benchmark/model citations. These broaden contextualization while preserving the original positioning. Venue/year updates for existing references are bibliographic changes, not new works.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits terminology and prose, adds discussion and acknowledgment sections, and reorganizes appendix material: for example, v1 Appendix K becomes v2 F.2, and v1 H becomes G.3. The framework is called three-stage rather than two-stage, matching the existing diagram. The core narrative and much of the original text remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds a runtime plot/table, cross-head bar chart, seed-comparison heatmaps, probe-comparison curves, and OLMo/SAE example displays. The former standalone insertion-strategy plot becomes Figure 6b alongside new general-performance panels. Existing displays are largely retained or relocated, with additional caption and table-formatting refinements.

improvement.justification: The new controlled comparisons and seed checks strengthen the existing empirical argument, while explicit attribution-scope limitations and the corrected ICL sign improve interpretation. The gains are tempered by qualitative-only OLMo/SAE validation, limited protocol detail for new evaluations, and a claim of statistically absent degradation without reported uncertainty. The probe-definition revision also leaves its relationship to the retained experimental results unexplained.
